rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Training platform = Claude Code (CLI + Desktop) + Cowork.
rules_evaluated.evidence: File names only 'Claude Code' throughout (Session widget L5 '(continue, ...)', three prompt-dest chips '(Claude Code)'); no `claude.ai` or Cowork-only feature named anywhere.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cloud/remote features carry Git dependency — out of scope for our training dir.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: no cloud/remote-feature claim (Routines, Claude Code on the web) made anywhere in this file

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Local scheduled tasks catch up on wake, but only once, only for runs missed in last 7 days.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: no scheduled-task / Desktop-routine claim in this file

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Verify capabilities BEFORE asserting, not after.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Expanded study prompt (fence 1): 'My Claude Code sessions across every project live under `~/.claude/projects/`, one folder per repo I've worked in.' This matches the compendium's own re-verified §6e fact verbatim in substance ('Claude Code stores session transcripts at `~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>/<uuid>.jsonl`, one folder per working directory') — the claim is a re-assertion of an already-verified compendium fact, not an unverified memory-drawn assertion.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Known correct Claude Code facts (easy to get wrong).
rules_evaluated.evidence: Study prompt's progress-update instruction — 'As you go, keep me posted: every thirty seconds or so, drop a quick line...' — phrases the cadence as a felt between-chunks habit ('or so'), matching §6's turn-streaming fact (no claim of literal concurrent narration during in-flight tool calls) and check_prompts.md §43's prescribed phrasing exactly. No plan-mode, connector, scheduling or subagent-dispatch claim contradicts §6 anywhere in the file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Transcript-by-mtime selection fragile when current session writes target folder.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Study prompt reads across ALL of `~/.claude/projects/` ('Read across them'), not a most-recent-mtime pick of a single file — the specific defect this rule guards (silently selecting the wrong file) can't arise from a breadth read across every folder.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Sessions = unit of work — write "start a new session in X," not "open Claude Code in X."
rules_evaluated.evidence: L5 '**Session** *(continue, "Module 6 worktree session")*' uses correct session-continuation vocabulary; no 'open Claude Code' phrasing anywhere in the file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cross-working-directory boundaries always open `new`; evidence travels by disk.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closing section 'Decide what crosses back to your main repo' (L57-59): 'The M5 worktree holds this module's work... Your main repo's copies stopped at the fork, stale rule and all.' Correctly frames the M5 worktree as a separate working directory whose gitignored artifacts (CLAUDE.local.md, observations/) do not cross automatically — matches §7b's evidence-travels-by-disk model. This exercise itself stays inside the already-open M6 worktree (Session widget says 'continue'), so no boundary crossing is asked of it here.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Same-cwd recovery defaults to `--resume`, not `new`.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L5 Session widget says 'continue' and body opens 'Same session as the gap map... in scrollback' — matches the same-cwd continuation default this rule prescribes; no session-reset asked mid-exercise.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Portability audits: analyze AGENT'S runtime, not prompt's literal syntax.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The `~/.claude/projects/` path in the study prompt sits inside a natural-language ask the agent itself reads and executes (Read/Grep tool calls it chooses), not literal shell text the student is told to type into their own terminal — matches §29's carve-out that agent-run paths are intent-illustration, not a portability risk needing de-bashing.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Prose describing a runtime the room never executes drifts to plausible mechanism.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest candidate, L55: 'The shapes stay in this session's scrollback; you build the handoff prompt from them.' States CONTEXT (shapes sit in scrollback) and what LANDS (feeds the handoff prompt) per §38's three-tell contract — no invented 'X against Y' retrieval mechanism, no borrowed lifecycle noun from a later stage, and the one cadence claim in the file ('every thirty seconds or so') is explicitly felt-cadence phrasing, not an unsourced wall-clock number.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Source URL + type label — mandatory.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Backing-block Sources (L90-91): curran-2x carries `[practitioner direct, vendor venue]` + URL; geoffintech-charles carries `[practitioner direct]` + URL — both below `<!-- maintainer -->`, per §1's body-exemption scope (body-grep for `https?://` = 0 hits, confirmed by body-view's `url` grep: body_hits 0, CLEAN). Body prose ('Expect the list to look familiar... The primitives Claude names are the ones your codebase already runs') carries no 'practitioners say' / 'entered the vocabulary' / convergence-verb framing. The one borderline phrase — 'the checking primitives the field already runs' (sidestep header + lead-in) — is covered by the maintainer's dated accept-note (L67, Antti 2026-09-02): 'the menu Claude returns reflects what is common in the field... Judges should not re-flag the header or the lead-in under check_research_claims.md §1.' Honored, not re-flagged.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Freshness rule — 6 months.
rules_evaluated.evidence: curran-2x: checked 2026-05-25, due 2026-10-16 — after today (2026-09-03). geoffintech-charles: checked 2026-05-25, due 2026-10-08 — also after today. Both inside their freshness window; neither uses `due:none` so §2a/§2b's durable-account tests don't apply.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Hold short OODA loose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Backing OODA roster (L104) names 5 practitioners; the Stance block (L98) already self-limits: 'Two named orgs plus an unnamed category does not clear the L3 bar' and 'no convergence verb attaches to this menu' — correctly does not overclaim convergence from a short roster.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Vision × Detail split.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All four backing Claims (L84-87) are explicitly labeled `vision` with `← none-owed`, correctly exempting them from KB-backing; the two Sources entries (L90-91) carry the KB backing for the detail-layer checking-primitives menu.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No "What research says" callout boxes.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L53 ships the sourced content as plain inline prose ('Expect the list to look familiar: ... Your list won't be exact.'), not a boxed 'research says' callout — matches the inline-builder-voice default.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Source-verification maintainer block on any student-facing file with practitioner citations.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Backing block's Sources section (L90-91) carries a per-source `[checked:... result:... due:...]` freshness stamp for both citations (per §11a's grammar) in place of a bare checklist — satisfies the verification-debt-visibility §11/§11a require.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Inference beyond source — absence licenses only absence.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Stance block (L97-99) names the limit rather than inferring past it: 'the menu is not convergent practitioner vocabulary... no convergence verb attaches to this menu. Do not reintroduce "convergent practitioner vocabulary" from any register.' No conclusion in body or backing goes beyond what the two sources support.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forcing functions stay, scripted reactions go. Forcing functions live in prompts, not body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The three forcing functions (scan-and-group, draw-as-diagrams, expand-and-rank the checking menu) all live in the prompt fences, not body prose. Body pacing callouts stay in suggestion register per §16's boundary clause: 'Once two or three recurring kinds of work are clear enough to draw and compare, move on. You do not need a complete inventory' (L26) and 'Fast operator? Lump the next two prompts into one go' (L24) are both opt-in suggestions, not bare imperative scripts ('two rounds max'-shaped).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No placeholders inside fences.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Grepped all three expanded prompt fences for `[BRACKETS]`-style placeholders (`grep -nE '\[[A-Z_ -]+\]|\[your |\[path |\[feature'`): zero hits. None of the three fences ends in a dangling colon awaiting student input either; all needed context (recurring groups, the dominant gap) is already in scrollback per §1's qualifier, so no open-hook is owed.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every prompt block: one-sentence action lead-in.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Word counts of the three lead-ins: 'Ask Claude to scan your sessions across every project and group the kinds of work that recur.' = 17 words; 'Ask Claude to draw your top few work-shapes as simple diagrams.' = 11 words; 'Ask Claude to name the checking primitives the field already runs and rank the ones that fit your gap.' = 19 words. All under the 20-word ceiling. The third's fuller length is justified under §2a's carve-out (a 4-paragraph prompt with two distinct moves — list-and-place primitives, then evaluate fit — genuinely needs a fuller cue than a 2-3 line prompt would). No fence ends in a dangling colon, so §2a's stricter sub-case doesn't apply.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Chain by back-reference + deterministic path, never invented alias.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Shapes prompt opens 'Take the recurring groups you just named' (explicit scrollback back-reference, no invented file path); primitives prompt opens 'Expand my menu of checks before I read my own map against it' and later references 'the dominant gap I named' — both anchor to prior-turn output via scrollback per this rule's preferred scrollback-chain style, never a file path that could drift.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Compendium platform claims rot at 60 days.
Maintain living capability notes for both runtimes; consult before asserting.
Don't extend known mechanism into adjacent context without verifying it fires there.
Fix the contract, not the broken recovery.
Practitioner observation beats docs lookup.
Live-test beats docs for runtime-behavior claims.
When tool feature behaves differently than expected, update curriculum -- not student's workaround.
Auto-load surface = SIX things.
Compendium pointers inside files = autoload-redundant.
PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks read env from harness, not from agent Bash subshells.
Edit-time prompt-edit gate's approval detector MUST parse the transcript deterministically.
CLAUDE.md describes runtime, not just task.
F-Secure curriculum off-limits.
No premature infrastructure.
External org content.
Destructive operations need confirmation.
No "as-is" imports from internet.
Pseudo-URI + kill-switch for public/private content split.
Bulk workbook rebuilds: derive flags from existing output, never guess "all."
Before auditing a built artifact ask whether it ships; before acting on a finding, re-measure it.
Internal audit/session-retro directories default-gitignore from creation.
Quality gates run at wind-down, not mid-session.
Tooling test layers carry acceptance-test contract.
Script ratchet -- every LLM-orchestration tooling surface ratchets toward script-replaceable assertions.
Hook lints partition into auto-fix vs warn.
Canon is declared, not inferred -- and an orphan is not automatically spent.
Runner <-> source pre-flight.
Judge must honor script exit codes.
Eval-fire writing-class fires must schema-validate before presenting verdicts.
Coverage tools enumerate universe, not index of past work.
Cowork sandboxed to its connected working directories.
`maintainer_acceptance` = JSON-level override for accepted/mitigated judge verdicts.
Quality stamps: tooling writes them; the SHA pins committed content.
Cowork capability surface -- UI surfaces subagent reads; no session rename in Cowork or Desktop.
Audit scope derives from TRAININGS registry + link-walk, not disk dir or tarball.
Acceptance-test contract covers prompt mechanics + end-state artefacts, NOT does prompt's executable shell actually work.
Strategy-doc drift surfaces via judge citation -- citation = canary, not verdict.
Skills at `~/.claude/skills/<name>/` are user-global but per-codebase in content -- namespace by SUT.
`state.json` files written by `run-mN.sh` are convenience caches, not authoritative.
tmux-runner sessions must use a per-runner socket.
A killed `run_in_background` Bash wrapper is not evidence the tmux session it launched is dead.
Spend on deleting the duplicate, not on guarding it -- and a gate that finds nothing is speculation.
`update-quality.sh` takes ALL classes in ONE invocation per file.
A hash guard is only as good as what it hashes, and a malformed hash disarms it silently.
Measure the defect before proposing the fix, and again before repeating it to the maintainer.
A judge subagent without evidence is a rubber-stamp, and the summary table cannot tell you which you got.
A gate keyed on the TOOL has a back door; a gate keyed on the FILE does not.
Harness-side caches drift; the artifact is canonical.
Before deleting anything, ask what its FIRING would look like.
A hook on a gitignored surface is a rule on ONE machine.
`git log -1 --date=short -- <path>` on a DELETED file returns the deletion date.
A detector's reading vocabulary must cover the corpus's writing vocabulary.
A verdict has more than one input; a freshness check usually watches one.
"It used to be fast" is a regression report -- diagnose it by trajectory, not by architecture.
A bench is silent about everything it cannot stage, and silence reads exactly like a pass.
An instruction whose violation leaves the output identical is not enforced by wording -- it needs a measurement or a test.
Thinking-effort levels are a real, named Claude Code control surface -- stamped.
OODA paraphrase != primary source.
Zombie stat guard.
Resist prescriptive post-OODA phrasings.
Default to asking before folding findings into strategy docs.
Grep `continuous-research/` and `memory/` before guessing at a name.
Consult research BEFORE generating, not after.
Denominator + axis discipline on every adoption/productivity number.
A green check must measure the fact, not a proxy that co-varies with it.
A word-presence claim needs an unprimed read.
A candidate that matches the hunt's SHAPE has not answered the hunt's QUESTION.
Rule in memory without forcing function = worse than no rule.
Short skeptical pushback on "done" = re-verify trigger.
Verification machinery needs smoke-test before trust.
Context-loading tiers as staged progression.
Multi-sample methods need structural enforcement.
Citation discipline -- extend cite-or-flag scope + quote supporting sentence.
